title: Manzanola Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Manzanola wells have a 40-foot median depth, with typical finished-well costs of $7,400-$14,200.
h1: Manzanola Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Well records around Manzanola show a mostly shallow plains-water setting, but the record is not uniform. Among 481 permitted wells within 5 miles, the median reported depth is 40 feet, and the median reported static water level is 18 feet. That makes local drilling look simpler than it may be on an individual lot.

Only 36 wells report a pump yield and 12 report a static water level, so these figures are useful for planning, not a guarantee. A driller still needs to evaluate the parcel, access, casing and grout requirements, pump equipment, and the intended household or irrigation use.

sections.heading: Manzanola’s shallow wells and the exceptions
sections.html:
Constructed well records near Manzanola have a median total depth of 40 feet. The middle half runs from 32 to 46 feet, and 94% of the depth records are under 100 feet. For a drilling bid, that points to a relatively short bore on many ordinary plains parcels.

There are important exceptions. The 90th percentile is 59 feet, while the deepest well on record is 1,550 feet. The depth mix also includes 2% between 100 and 300 feet and 4% at 600 feet or more. Local geology, the exact lot, intended use, and drilling conditions can change the estimate sharply.

sections.heading: What Manzanola wells make for water
sections.html:
The reported yield numbers are unusually strong, with a median of 275 gallons per minute and a middle half from 15 to 802.5 gallons per minute. Of the wells that report yield, 81% are listed above 15 gallons per minute, while 19% fall between 5 and 15 gallons per minute.

Do not treat the median as a promise for a new household well. Only 36 wells report pump yield, and irrigation wells can produce very differently from domestic wells. Ask for a pumping test or nearby completion information. An exempt household-use well is generally limited to 35 gallons per minute for pumping, even if the aquifer can produce more.

sections.heading: Water levels around Manzanola
sections.html:
The 12 wells with static water-level records show a median depth to water of 18 feet, with the middle half between 10 and 21 feet. Those measurements suggest that water is commonly encountered fairly shallowly in the local record, which helps explain the shallow well-depth pattern.

There is not enough decade-by-decade static-water-level information in these records to call a rising or falling long-term water-table trend. A buyer should not infer that the water level will be the same on every parcel. Seasonal conditions, pumping nearby, well construction, and the exact alluvial or sedimentary setting can matter more than the area median.

sections.heading: Who has drilled near Manzanola, and when
sections.html:
Permit activity extends across the area’s history rather than being limited to recent growth. Records show 52 permits in the 1950s, 49 in the 1960s, 20 in the 1970s, 19 in the 1980s, 53 in the 1990s, 44 in the 2000s, 40 in the 2010s, and 13 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025.

The most frequent driller names in the records are Crandall, H A with 48 wells, Broce Drilling with 19, and Parrish Drilling with 13. These names help with local research, but a historical permit does not establish current availability or guarantee a result.

sections.heading: What a new Manzanola well may cost
sections.html:
The local cost model uses a typical drilling rate of $35-$55 per foot for alluvium and plains sedimentary rock. At the 40-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to roughly $1,400-$2,200. That is the hole only, not the complete water system.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at $7,400-$14,200. Your quote can move outside that range if the site needs unusual casing or grout, deeper drilling, difficult access, longer trenching, treatment, or more involved electrical work. Have the driller separate drilling, completion, pump, and site-work allowances in writing.

sections.heading: Manzanola risks to check before closing
sections.html:
Yield is not the only risk. The mapped area within about 10 miles includes 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 2 historic mine features, and 3 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. That does not prove a problem at a particular parcel, but it supports checking environmental records and testing water before relying on it.

The permits name an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer on 465 wells, Alluvial on 5, and Quaternary Alluvium on 5; 0 are Denver Basin aquifer wells. Confirm the permit status and allowed use with Colorado DWR. For a home, also plan septic setbacks, a suitable drainfield area, legal access for drilling equipment, and enough room for the well, pressure system, and future repairs.

sections.heading: Buying or building near Manzanola
sections.html:
Before purchasing, obtain the permit and construction record for the subject well and compare nearby wells in Manzanola, Olney Springs, Crowley, Fowler, Rocky Ford, Ordway, and Sugar City. The nearby records can show how variable depth, construction, use, and reported yield may be across the plains.

For vacant land, make the water plan part of due diligence rather than assuming the 40-foot median applies to the lot. Confirm a legal water supply, an approvable septic layout, equipment access, and the expected electrical route. If the parcel will support irrigation, livestock, or a new home, have a qualified contractor and the water-rights professionals review those uses before you close.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Manzanola, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Manzanola is 40 feet. The middle half of wells is 32 to 46 feet, and 94% are under 100 feet. Conditions vary, though: the deepest recorded well is 1,550 feet, so nearby records are a planning guide rather than a guarantee for a specific parcel.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Manzanola?
faq.a: The local model uses $35-$55 per foot. At the 40-foot median depth, the drilled hole is about $1,400-$2,200. A completed system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at $7,400-$14,200. Access, casing, grout, depth, and site conditions can move an actual proposal outside that range.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Manzanola?
faq.a: Among the 36 wells with reported pump yield, the median is 275 gallons per minute, with a middle half from 15 to 802.5 gallons per minute. The records are dominated by irrigation and other uses, so that result should not be used as a household guarantee. Request a pumping test or comparable domestic-well data.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Manzanola?
faq.a: The well records do not establish drinking-water safety. Within about 10 miles, mapped sites include 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 2 historic mine features, and 3 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Test the specific well for relevant contaminants, bacteria, and basic water chemistry, especially before occupying or buying a home.

faq.q: Do Manzanola wells have a falling water table?
faq.a: The available records show a median static water level of 18 feet, with the middle half from 10 to 21 feet. Only 12 wells report static water level, so the data do not support a reliable rising or falling trend by decade. Check recent measurements from nearby wells and account for season, pumping, and the exact location.
